topSpeedMPS.citation: Frontiers in Sports & Active Living, 2024, ages 9-11 on-ice combine test, n=11 male: 15.2m sprint peak speed 7.60+/-0.32 m/s. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11358090/

accel0to10mS.citation: PMC11358090 reports a 6.1m acceleration split of 1.53+/-0.19s, not a 10m split. Scaled to 10m via sqrt(distance) ratio: 1.53 * sqrt(10/6.1) = 1.959s. A kinematic scaling of real data, not an independent estimate.

avgAccelMPS2.citation: Computed from accel0to10mS via kinematics (d = 0.5*a*t^2, d=10m).

turningRadiusM.citation: No published turning-radius figure exists at any age, including this one despite real speed/accel data. Estimated as v^2 / (0.6 * avgAccelMPS2) -- see docs/scenario-engine/physics-sourcing.md for the assumption.

stoppingDistanceM.citation: No published stopping-distance figure exists at any age. Estimated as v^2 / (2 * avgAccelMPS2), assuming braking capability comparable to acceleration capability.

reactionDelayS.citation: No ice-hockey or youth-hockey reaction-time study exists at any age. 250-350ms range built from adult non-hockey athlete proxy data (PMC11207928) per docs/scenario-engine/physics-sourcing.md, applied flat across all bands since no age-hockey curve exists in the literature.

passSpeedMPS.citation: No youth ice-hockey pass-velocity study exists. Scaled from the U18 pass-speed reference (18 m/s, itself well below the cited adult 70mph+ shot lower bound) by this band's real topSpeedMPS ratio to U18's, as an athletic-development proxy.

iceDecelerationMPS2.citation: mu*g using Alain Hache's puck-on-ice sliding friction coefficient (~0.1, https://physicsworld.com/a/physics-on-ice/) and standard gravity (9.81 m/s^2). Real, age-independent physical constant.
